note: Rebuilt on every run of .github/workflows/daily-creator-pull.yml from the hooks harvested that day. Spyglass HOOK/USP aggregation returns empty for these creators because it is tuned to paid campaigns, so the patterns are read off the organic hooks themselves. Every quote is verified against a harvested hook before it is written.

patterns.label: announces a correction without giving it
patterns.description: Declares that a widely held belief is wrong, or that a familiar term is misused, but withholds the actual correction — an information gap opened in a single sentence.

examples.creator: Jack Henderson
examples.quote: Here's something people don't understand.

examples.creator: Wealth | Wisdom | Daily
examples.quote: Your first rental feels like freedom, and that's the part that confuses people.

examples.creator: Sean Pan
examples.quote: Real estate investors love throwing around terms like cash on cash return.

examples.creator: Jerry Norton
examples.quote: Although wholesaling as a strategy may be simple to understand, it isn't easy to execute.

patterns.label: states where the viewer is right now
patterns.description: Opens by describing the viewer's present circumstances in second person as plain fact, which lands as a personal address and implies the video is about to change that situation.

examples.creator: Wealth | Wisdom | Daily
examples.quote: Right now, you pay rent to someone else.

examples.creator: Erick Brice
examples.quote: You're 20 years old.

examples.creator: Scott Betley
examples.quote: How much are y 'all paying for rent right now?

patterns.label: leads with the dollar outcome
patterns.description: Puts a concrete figure or achieved result in the first clause and defers the method, so the number does the stopping and the unanswered 'how' does the holding.

examples.creator: Sean Pan
examples.quote: I bought this 4plex for $250,000 and this is how much I make from it.

examples.creator: Jeremy Werden
examples.quote: Five years ago, we turned this into North Carolina's number one Airbnb.

examples.creator: 𝘾𝘼𝙈𝙀𝙍𝙊𝙉 𝙊𝙇𝙄𝙑𝙀𝙍𝘼  📍ℂ𝕙𝕚𝕔𝕒𝕘𝕠
examples.quote: Whenever me and my boy need to make $5,000, this is what we do.

patterns.label: drops you into a conversation already running
patterns.description: Starts on a fragment that clearly belongs to the middle of something — a transition, an aside, a reply — so the viewer feels they walked in late and scrolls back rather than away.

examples.creator: Jerry Norton
examples.quote: Okay, so the next thing I need to talk about some earnest money, man,

examples.creator: Michael Llanas
examples.quote: I have a question now

examples.creator: 𝘾𝘼𝙈𝙀𝙍𝙊𝙉 𝙊𝙇𝙄𝙑𝙀𝙍𝘼  📍ℂ𝕙𝕚𝕔𝕒𝕘𝕠
examples.quote: You had a closed deal today?

patterns.label: a blunt order not to do something
patterns.description: Opens with a flat negative command before any context, so the viewer has to keep watching to find out why the rule exists and whether they are already breaking it.

examples.creator: Logan Fullmer
examples.quote: Never ever ever buy houses listed on the market.

examples.creator: Jeremy Werden
examples.quote: Do not buy a lakefront or beachfront property unless you consider this.

patterns.label: promises a payoff for finishing
patterns.description: Frames the video itself as the deal: stay to the end, or belong to this group, and you get a stated advantage. The reward is named before any content is given.

examples.creator: Theoni Rapo
examples.quote: If you can make it through this whole entire video, you will be smarter than any other person that's buying real estate for the rest of 2026.

examples.creator: Scott Betley
examples.quote: If you're hoping to buy a home in the coming years, this is hands down one of the best strategies you can use to put yourself in an incredible financial position when you buy a home.

patterns.label: opens on a question from someone else
patterns.description: The first line is a question put to the creator rather than by the creator, which casts the video as an answer owed to a real person and borrows the asker's curiosity.

examples.creator: Ravi Sharma
examples.quote: When you have spare money in smaller amounts, around 20 to 50K, would you save it towards your next deposit or try to do a cosmetic reno to manufacture some equity?

examples.creator: Sean Pan
examples.quote: Does it matter if you intend to have like housemates and stuff like that?

patterns.label: asks the question they already typed
patterns.description: Opens with the exact beginner question the target viewer has searched for, sometimes narrowed to an oddly specific price and place, which signals the video is a direct answer to their query.

examples.creator: Fernando Gonzalez
examples.quote: ¿Cómo empezar a invertir en bienes raíces?

examples.creator: Scott Betley
examples.quote: Have you ever wondered how much money you actually need to make to buy a $259 ,000 home in Harford County, Maryland?

patterns.label: opens with bad news about the market
patterns.description: Leads with a sweeping claim about conditions getting worse, often framed as unprecedented or still in motion, so the viewer stays to learn how exposed they are.

examples.creator: Scott Kuru
examples.quote: For the first time, a government is actively trying to sink the housing market, which is the biggest investment most Aussies will ever make in their lives.

examples.creator: Ravi Sharma
examples.quote: Interest rates have gone up and they're about to go up again.

patterns.label: introduces a stranger and a date
patterns.description: Opens on a specific third party at a specific past moment — an analyst, a client at lunch — which sets up a story with an outcome the viewer has to wait for.

examples.creator: Avery Carl
examples.quote: Seven months ago, this housing analyst predicted a crash worse than 2008, with home prices eventually falling as much as 50%.

examples.creator: Jack Henderson
examples.quote: I had a lunch with a private wealth client the other day who's almost 70.

patterns.label: points at the deal on screen
patterns.description: Anchors the hook to a single concrete thing in frame — this property, this contract — so the promised breakdown feels verifiable rather than theoretical.

examples.creator: Jack Henderson
examples.quote: When it comes to a property that can take advantage of all of the new tax concessions, like the capital gains tax discount, like negative gearing, and get massive depreciation benefits, they don't get much better than this property right here.

examples.creator: 𝘾𝘼𝙈𝙀𝙍𝙊𝙉 𝙊𝙇𝙄𝙑𝙀𝙍𝘼  📍ℂ𝕙𝕚𝕔𝕒𝕘𝕠
examples.quote: To get this one contract signed, let's break down the numbers.

patterns.label: warns one specific group of buyers
patterns.description: Flags a caveat aimed at people already committed to a particular plan or product, which filters the audience and makes those inside it unable to scroll past.

examples.creator: Scott Betley
examples.quote: Just a quick PSA, if you're planning to use an FHA loan to buy a home,

examples.creator: Avery Carl
examples.quote: Sometimes vacation rentals are very highly regulated

patterns.label: begins inside a real phone call
patterns.description: Single example. The hook is the first line of an actual script being performed on a live call, so the viewer is watching the thing happen rather than hearing it described.

examples.creator: Jerry Norton
examples.quote: Hi Peter, my name is Jerry Norton calling you about your property on Liberty Road.

patterns.label: acts out the excuse people make
patterns.description: Single example. The creator performs the viewer's objection as dialogue, complete with the sigh, so the rest of the video becomes a rebuttal the viewer already feels implicated in.

examples.creator: Fernando Gonzalez
examples.quote: Ay, es que necesito ser rico para comenzar a invertir en bienes raíces.
